title: Latency economics and tiered routing playbook
author: Priya Nanduri
body:
Overview

Purpose
This playbook defines the design, operational controls, and experiment/runbook procedures for latency-aware, cost-conscious tiered routing in the Redwood serving runtime. It connects SLO targets, per-tenant economics, and fallback policies so routing decisions preserve customer-facing latency SLOs while minimizing unit cost.

Scope
- Applies to multi-tenant hosted and Dedicated pools where requests may be routed across model variants, regions, and capacity tiers.
- Not intended to replace per-customer contractual routing written in the control plane (those are higher-level policies implemented using these primitives).

Goals and design constraints
1) SLO preservation: prioritize meeting 99th percentile latency objectives for customer-facing routes.
2) Cost sensitivity: route to lower-cost model variants or capacity tiers when doing so will not materially violate SLOs or degrade quality beyond tolerance.
3) Safety: provide deterministic fallbacks and observability to avoid routing flaps and oscillation.
4) Incremental deployability: new routing heuristics must be testable against shadow traffic and staged canaries.

Key concepts and terminology
- Tier: a logical grouping of capacity (e.g., premium-dedicated, shared-hosted, burst-spot).
- Model variant: exact model artifact plus quantization/precision profile (e.g., gptx-1.2-int8-v2).
- Fidelity: qualitative measure of expected output quality for a given variant.
- Cost-per-token (CPT): estimated operator cost for serving a token on a given variant/tier.
- Latency budget: per-request remaining time to meet the configured SLO.
- Route policy: declarative rule combining selectors (tenant, route, weight) and decision predicates.

Routing decision flow (high-level)
1. Admission: validate request metadata, tenant allowances, and route-level constraints.
2. Classification: tag request with workload profile (sequence-length estimate, sync/async, priority).
3. Candidate generation: list compatible model variants and tiers.
4. Scoring: compute score for each candidate: score = alpha * latency_score + beta * cost_score + gamma * fidelity_penalty.
5. Selection and reservation: pick highest-scoring candidate that satisfies hard predicates (region affinity, contractual pinning). Reserve slot capacity (kernel admission).
6. Execution and post-eval: if execution violates latency budget or quality regression, trigger fallback/rollback.

SLO and economics math (practical formulae)
- Expected latency per candidate L_c = median_kernel_latency(candidate, shape) + network_estimate(candidate.region). Use histogram-backed estimates.
- Cost per request R_c = CPT(candidate) * expected_tokens(request). For batching, use amortized cost models (see amortized_cost_table below).
- Composite utility U_c = (SLO_headroom(c)/SLO_target) - lambda * (R_c / R_ref) - mu * FidelityPenalty(c). We treat SLO_headroom as max(0, SLO_target - E[L_c]).
- Decision threshold: pick candidate with max U_c subject to U_c > U_min else route to fallback (higher tier).

Config table (example values)
|| key || description || example || notes ||
|| slo.target || target latency (ms) for route || 95 ms (P99) || route-level override ||
|| lambda || cost weight in utility || 0.8 || tuned per product vertical ||
|| mu || fidelity penalty weight || 1.2 || fidelity penalty normalized [0,1] ||
|| U_min || minimal acceptable utility || -0.2 || prevents overly cheap but slow picks ||
|| cost_ref || normalization constant for cost || $0.0005/token || updated by billing team weekly ||

Operational rules and safety knobs
- Circuit-breaker: if the selected candidate's observed P99 exceeds slo.target + 20% for 5 mins, route flow is temporarily pinned to next-safe tier and an alert is fired (severity P2).
- Dampening window: do not switch routing preference for a tenant more than once per 60s to avoid oscillation.
- Shadow testing: new candidate variants must be validated by 1 hour of 10% shadow traffic before being eligible for live routing.
- Canary rollout: initial 1% of live traffic with metric-based escalation gates (latency, quality regression).

Runbook: outage or mass-latency incident (step-by-step)
1. Detect: Pager triggers from latency SLO alert (P99 exceeded for > 3m across a route).
2. Triage: identify which candidate types account for majority of slow requests (use the routing decisions histogram - see observability queries section).
3. Immediate mitigation (fast path): enable route-level override to force-route to premium-dedicated variant or raise U_min to deprioritize low-cost candidates. Command-line: 

sh
redwoodctl routes override set --route customer.chat --variant premium-gptx-1 --reason "p99-latency-spike"

4. Validate: watch P99 and token drop rates for 10m. If steady, keep override while root cause investigation continues.
5. Permanent remediation: revert to automated routing only after corrective changes (kernel patch, region failover, or cost recalibration) and a successful canary run.

Telemetry & observability contract
Minimum signals required for safe operation and postmortem:
- per-route, per-variant P50/P95/P99 latency histograms (1s bucketing for 1m window)
- per-route request counts and error counts by variant and tier
- candidate selection reasons (why candidate selected: lowest cost / fidelity / pinned)
- route decision churn metric (switches/min per tenant)
- shadow validation pass/fail rates and quality regression counts
- amortized cost per request and per-token CPI-like metric

Example observability queries (PromQL-like pseudocode)
- P99 latency for route "customer.chat":
redwood_latency_seconds_bucket{route="customer.chat",job="runtime"} -> histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(...)))
- Fraction of requests routed to low-cost tier:
sum(rate(requests_total{tier="shared"} [5m])) / sum(rate(requests_total[5m]))

Quality safety and fidelity checks
- Automatic prompt-level checks: for generation routes with fidelity-sensitive SLAs, run lightweight rerank/consistency checks in shadow before returning low-fidelity results live. If rerank confidence < threshold, fall back to higher-fidelity variant.
- Regression window: if quality metric delta exceeds 1.5x baseline for 10m, pin variant and trigger remediation.

Operational exercises and experiments (lab recipes)
Each experiment below should be scheduled in the runtime lab environment and follow the experiment governance checklist (owned, hypothesis, rollback, telemetry).
1. Cost-pressure response drill
   - Hypothesis: under sustained increase in cost_ref by 25%, routing will shift to cheaper variants without violating P99.
   - Steps: bump lambda to 1.6 for a test tenant, enable shadowing for new variants, monitor P99, fidelity.
   - Success: no >10% increase in P99 and fidelity regression < threshold.
2. Synthetic tail latency injection
   - Hypothesis: the dampening window prevents oscillation when kernels degrade intermittently.
   - Steps: inject 200 ms additional kernel tail for candidate A for 7m and observe routing churn.
   - Success: churn < 0.5 switches/min and circuit-breaker triggers if needed.
3. Canary for new quantized variant
   - Steps: 10% shadow -> 1% live -> 5% live -> 20% live; at each stage validate latency, quality, cost.

Rollout checklist for routing policy changes
- Author a policy PR including: policy YAML, target routes, and experiment plan.
- Run 1 hour of shadow validation on staging with traffic representative of production (latency and token shape).
- Create a canary run for a pilot tenant for 24h with automatic rollback gates for P99 and quality.
- Post-canonicalization: add telemetry enrichment and update billing/cost models if CPT adjustments required.

Ownership and escalation
- Policy author (owner): eng-serving-runtime/routing (primary)
- Oncall escalation: runtime SRE -> runtime platform lead -> product owner for route
- SLA incident owner: whoever owns the route in the Console product mapping table.

Appendices
A. Example policy YAML (simplified)

---
route: customer.chat
slo:
  p99_ms: 95
  emergency_fallback_ms: 200
policies:
  - id: prefer_low_cost_with_headroom
    selectors:
      - tenant_tier: standard
    scoring:
      lambda: 0.8
      mu: 1.2
      alpha: 0.6
    predicates:
      - region_affinity: true
      - fidelity_min: 0.85
    safety:
      shadow_validation: 1h
      dampening_seconds: 60
---

B. Amortized cost note
- When batching occurs, compute amortized CPT by dividing measured kernel execution cost by average batch size observed in the same time window. This prevents underestimating cost for low-latency but small-batch shapes.

C. Related diagnostics (runbook quick commands)
- Show recent routing decision histogram (last 15m):
redwoodctl metrics query --name routing_decisions_histogram --route customer.chat --since 15m
- Force a policy override:
redwoodctl routes override set --route customer.chat --policy "pin-premium" --reason "p99-spike"

D. Change log
